conventions.convention: The pivotal map is j=uθ, and dimensions and Hopf-link entries use its spherical pivotal trace. Modularity means invertibility of the unnormalized double-braiding matrix s. In general D is either square root of Σ d_i²; positivity and unitarity are not assumed.
Pointed category data include the associator ω, both hexagons for r, duality maps, ribbon twist q, and a compatible pivotal structure with every simple dimension equal to one.
The Walker Maslov form is ψ([a],[a′])=ω(a,b′), where a+b+c=0. It uses the stated quotient by adjacent intersections and its nondegenerate signature.
Bordism relations satisfy j₀x₀=j₁x₁ in the individual bordism. Composition adds n₂+n₁+μ(Aλ₀,λ₁,Bᵗλ₂), computed in the actual middle surface.
Connected state spaces are Hom(1,W₁⊗⋯⊗W_n⊗H^g), with H=⊕_i i⊗i*. Empty tensor powers are the unit; disconnected surfaces use tensor products, with empty value C.
Geometric cap pairing in composition-dual coordinates is Q_i=D^(g−1)/d(i), with inverse N_i=D^(1−g)d(i). This differs from the categorical trace d_i².

Boundary orientations are outward-normal-first. The actual stacked surgery signature defect is +μ_W in the canonical middle-object orientation. Weight acts by κ^n, with the specified cap-reference correction for arbitrary real Lagrangians.

Relative surgery comparisons retain the specified output identification and fixed component partition. O3 permits an arbitrary integer-framed knot with its small disk-zero meridian; graphs also require slides over the actual surgery longitudes.
The SU(2) family uses every integer ℓ≥3, q=exp(πi/ℓ), positive pivotal dimensions, twists q^(a(a+2)/2), and the positive square root of D².

Fusion matrices have rows indexed by the second input and columns by output. Verlinde uses the dual label k* without complex conjugation. The positive Hopf generator gives (ST)³=κI; the inverse generator gives (S⁻¹T)³=κC.

load_bearing.statement: Assume full AC. Every specified compact oriented collared decorated three-bordism has a marked fixed-base surgery presentation; any two such presentations realize their specified output identification by finite O1/O2/O3 moves, exterior framed isotopies and graph-strand slides, retaining coupons, collars and the fixed component partition.
For the actual standard-cap stacking presentations, Δσ=μ_W(R₁α₀,α₁,R₂ᵗα₂). The stated cap-reference integer satisfies a(BA)−a(B)−a(A)=μ_α−μ_λ; Z(M,n;λ)=κ^(n+a)Z_α(M) composes with n_comp=n₂+n₁+μ_λ.

The standard capped-cylinder Gram form is Q_t(y_j,x_i)=δ_ij D^(g−1)d(i)⁻¹y_ix_i, with inverse correction N_t|_i=D^(1−g)d(i). The normalized fixed-presentation maps satisfy the exact stacked law with factor κ^(σ(B₁)+σ(B₂)−σ(B_comp)), including disconnected cases.

The entire graph evaluation is unchanged under a framed band slide of one Ω-colored surgery component over another, or an arbitrary fixed-color open graph strand over an Ω component, retaining all exterior factors and actual coupons.
K_±(X)=p_±θ_X^∓¹, E_X=D²P_X, and R_ij(E_(i*⊗j))=δ_ij(D²/d_i)1_(i⊗i*); normalized evaluations are unchanged under signed twist surgery and arbitrary-knot circumcision.
For composable finite-dimensional real Lagrangian relations, m(B,A)=μ(Aλ₀,λ₁,Bᵗλ₂) satisfies m(B,A)+m(C,BA)=m(C,B)+m(CB,A), without injectivity, transversality or equal-dimension assumptions.

Assume full AC. The supplied generic adapted function path admits a descending family with prescribed admissible endpoint fields, no index-increasing ordinary trajectories, finitely many separated transverse same-index passages, protected birth neighborhoods and smooth framed elementary-band data through positive-drop tangencies.

Assume AC. Two specified all-two-handle presentations joined by the supplied finite based mixed-handle movie are related in the fixed base by finite exterior framed isotopies and O2/O3 moves, with the cumulative outgoing map prescribed by that movie.
Assume AC. The signature induces an isomorphism σ:Ω₄^SO→Z whose inverse sends 1 to the complex-oriented projective plane; a zero-signature closed oriented smooth four-manifold itself bounds.
For the stated complex modular ribbon fusion category, s²=D²C. In particular D²≠0, and S=s/D satisfies S²=C.
N_ij^k=Σ_x S_ix S_jx S_(k* x)/S_0x, and N_iS=S diag(S_ix/S_0x), for the explicitly stated row/column convention, without complex conjugation.

Assume full AC. The stated exact surgery operators define a presentation-independent symmetric monoidal weighted RT functor for every complex modular ribbon fusion category, preserving duality and admitting both geometric sewing inverses, including disconnected bordisms, empty ends, actual coupons and arbitrary real object Lagrangians.

concerns.concern: F2 and step 2.1 apply relative Hurewicz to the actual pair consisting of the contractible path total and its strict loop fiber. The cited thm-relative-hurewicz-theorem assumes a CW pair; no CW-pair structure on this actual pair is established. The loop supplier gives CW homotopy type of the fiber, which alone is not the cited pair hypothesis. A short explicit comparison using the cone on a marked CW fiber model and naturality of the pair sequences would justify the intended generator calculation.

The Statement calls p_+=1+i and p_-=1−i the 'normalized Gauss sums'. These are the unnormalized sums Σ θ_i^±1 d_i² used throughout the A page; the normalized values are p_±/D. The numerical calculations and subsequent normalization factors are consistent.

alerts.finding: Published supplier lem-circle-and-path-loop-models-for-eilenberg-maclane-induction, F4: 'Schön, Proposition 3, states that the fiber of a Hurewicz fibration has CW homotopy type when its total and base spaces have CW homotopy type.' Step 2.1 then says 'Apply [F4] to the Hurewicz fibration of step 1.2: its strict loop fiber has CW homotopy type.' F4 is an external source assertion, not a proved local supplier, and the item supplies no local argument establishing this CW-type theorem. Its brief description of Schön's proof does not construct or prove the required CW-type replacement. Thus the published proof has an unmet local prerequisite under the active local-proof rule. Batch 78 uses this precise conclusion in the integral Eilenberg–Mac Lane induction. This finding concerns local proof support, not a counterexample to the mathematical CW-type conclusion.
